page: Microsoft Azure E64s_v5 is a memory-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. It features 64 vCPUs built on 32 physical cores with hyperthreading and dedicated CPU allocation. The instance is equipped with 512 GB of RAM, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU memory ratio. Hardware instruction sets include AVX-512, VNNI, AES, and SHA_NI acceleration. There is no local instance storage included, though it supports attached Premium Storage.

Benchmark evaluation reveals high multi-core performance and strong memory bandwidth. In multi-threaded CPU suites like PassMark and stress-ng, as well as multi-core Geekbench, the instance places in the top quartile. Large-block memory throughput reaches 296.85 GB/sec for uncached reads and 136.92 GB/sec for writes. Database operations, Redis SET workloads processing 62.15 million operations per second, and static web serving tests all register in the top 25 percent performance band. Single-core processing across Geekbench and compression tasks yields average performance.

LLM inference testing shows moderate throughput for small and medium parameters, while large 70B model text generation falls into the bottom 25 percent due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. Cost efficiency is driven by high memory density and strong multi-core scalability, offering solid value for memory-bound and multi-threaded enterprise workloads without paying for unneeded local ephemeral disks. Ideal applications include large in-memory databases, Redis caches, enterprise database operations, software compilation, and heavy web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure E64s_v5 is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by a 32-core Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, supplying 64 dedicated vCPUs and 512 GB of RAM. Designed without local storage, it relies on attached Premium Storage capabilities. Hardware acceleration features include AVX-512, VNNI, and cryptographic extensions. Benchmarks demonstrate strong multi-core processing power, memory bandwidth, and high throughput in Redis SET operations and enterprise database tasks, placing in the top quartile among tested servers. Single-threaded benchmarks and LLM processing fall within average tiers, with large-model text generation constrained by CPU-only execution. The 8 GB per vCPU ratio makes the instance cost-effective for memory-intensive enterprise tasks. It is well suited for large in-memory caching systems, relational databases, software compilation, and high-concurrency web applications.
